baseline.name: Separate presence bitmap
baseline.approach: Mark every observed value in a new n-element bitmap, then emit unmarked positions.

archived.name: Sign marks stored in the input
archived.space: O(1) marking workspace plus an O(n) allocated output buffer

why: The sign of each input slot serves as its visited flag, removing the separate presence array.
quantitative_comparison: The archive avoids n presence flags but still allocates n result integers. Both perform two linear passes, so total memory remains O(n) when returned storage is counted; no time advantage is measured.
tradeoffs: Input signs are modified, values must lie in 1..n, and allocation/abs bounds are trusted. A preserving baseline may be preferable when callers need the original data.
evidence_basis: Static storage-accounting comparison, separating auxiliary and returned memory; no benchmark.
